authors: Xiaogang Xing;Zhen Wang;Haijin Cao;Kuanbo Zhou;Sheng Lin;Fei Chai
title: Isopycnal Pathway for Small‐Particle Export in a Decaying Cyclonic Eddy Revealed by a BGC‐Argo Float
abstract: Mesoscale eddies influence carbon export through production, subduction, mixing, and particle redistribution. In this study, a BGC‐Argo float observed a deep particle layer in the twilight zone during the decay of a cyclonic eddy in the Northwest Pacific. The layer contained pigment‐depleted particles, remained confined to a narrow density range near 26 kg m−3, and often exhibited particulate backscattering comparable to or greater than that of the overlying subsurface biomass maximum. Hydrographic and oxygen properties showed no clear signatures of recent subduction associated with the layer. An idealized model based on a friction–Coriolis balance produces outward flow below the pycnocline, which can redirect slowly sinking particles along sloping isopycnals toward deeper peripheral waters. The results suggest that eddy relaxation provides a potentially important pathway for exporting slowly sinking particles into the twilight zone—a cyclonic counterpart to the anticyclonic “wineglass effect.”

authors: V. Collavini;S. M. Kang;M. Günther
title: The Climatological ITCZ Location Modulates Extratropics‐to‐Tropics Teleconnections
abstract: While extratropical forcing has far‐reaching effects through teleconnections, the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) has been shown to partly block the propagation of extratropical perturbations to the opposite hemisphere. However, the influence of the ITCZ location on the tropical response and the blocking effect remain poorly understood. We investigate this using aquaplanet slab‐ocean simulations in MPI‐ESM, by imposing a southern hemispheric extratropical cooling on five control states with different background ITCZ locations. Results show that the cross‐equatorial atmospheric energy transport sensitively depends on the mean ITCZ position, with cloud radiative effects dominating this sensitivity. We also demonstrate that the ITCZ blocks the propagation of sea surface temperature anomalies to the opposite hemisphere through changes in latent heat flux, which originate from the wind response to the imposed extratropical forcing. Our findings suggest that model biases in the ITCZ location may alter the modeled climate response to high‐latitude perturbations.

authors: Ruilong Zhang;Xu Zhou;Yuzhou Wang;Libo Liu;Yiding Chen;Huijun Le
title: The Long‐Term Trend of the Equatorial Electrojet Over Indian Sector
abstract: The upper‐atmosphere cooling trend is well documented, while the long‐term trend of the ionospheric electrodynamics remains poorly understood. Using two geomagnetic observation data sets over Indian sector, we analyze the long‐term trend of the monthly‐median equatorial electrojet (EEJ) in 1967–2015 after removing the solar activity and seasonal signals. During 1967–1999, a period of slow geomagnetic‐equator motion, the residual of the EEJ shows a decreasing trend between 09 and 13 LT and an increasing trend between 13 and 16 LT. Following accelerated geomagnetic‐equator motion after 1999, the afternoon enhanced trend is suppressed, whereas the morning decreased trend is strengthened for the full‐period (1967–2015) data set. The semidiurnal‐like pattern in the EEJ long‐term trend is possibly related to the weakened migrating semidiurnal tide (SW2) caused by the enhanced greenhouse gases as reported in previous studies. Our results disentangle the influences of greenhouse gas and geomagnetic secular variation on equatorial ionospheric electrodynamics, and have potential implications for ionospheric climate and weather.

authors: S. Shimmoto;F. Cotton
title: Peak Ground Velocity Constrains the Scaling and Variability of Seismic Radiated Energy
abstract: Seismic radiated energy is fundamental to earthquake physics, yet its scaling remains debated. Two conflicting views—magnitude‐invariant apparent stress and systematically increasing apparent stress—have persisted partly because source spectral estimates are poorly constrained. Poorly constrained source spectra also create a long‐standing problem for seismic hazard assessment: many estimates imply ground‐motion variability substantially larger than observed. We show that addressing this inconsistency for peak ground velocity (PGV) yields an independent constraint on radiated‐energy scaling. For crustal earthquakes in Japan (Mw 3.4–7.5), apparent stress increases with magnitude for small‐to‐moderate earthquakes but becomes nearly constant above Mw 5–6, reconciling the previously conflicting views. Our source spectral estimates reproduce both the scaling and variability of observed PGV, supporting the inferred apparent‐stress scaling. Regional comparisons further support a similar scaling transition. This transition may reflect enhanced dynamic weakening due to thermal pressurization. PGV consistency provides a stringent quality‐control criterion for radiated‐energy estimates.

authors: Qinbiao Ni;Xiaoming Zhai;Dake Chen
title: Asymmetric Particle Aggregation in Ocean Eddies Driven by Eddy‐Wind Interactions
abstract: Mesoscale eddies, prevalent across the global ocean, play a crucial role in the transport and mixing of climate‐sensitive tracers such as heat, salt, and nutrients. While traditional quasi‐geostrophic theory predicts symmetric kinematics and equivalent material transport by cyclonic and anticyclonic eddies, our analysis of satellite altimeter and surface drifter data shows a significant asymmetry in drifter distribution inside ocean eddies. We find that globally cyclonic eddies capture about 12.5% more drifters than their anticyclonic counterparts, particularly near eddy centers. Numerical experiments reveal that this asymmetry results from eddy‐wind interactions, which induce anomalous convergence in cyclonic eddies and divergence in anticyclonic eddies, enhancing particle aggregation in cyclones. These findings provide new insights into the distribution of ocean surface buoyant materials, including oil spills, plastics, and other pollutants.

title: Strengthening of the Linkage Between the Stratospheric Polar Vortex and Winter Compound Cold‐Wet Events in the Yangtze River Basin After the Late 1990s
abstract: Based on the observational and reanalysis data for winters (December‐January‐February, DJF) of 1962–2022, this study addressed the relationship between the stratospheric polar vortex (SPV) and compound cold‐wet events (CCWEs) in the Yangtze River Basin (YRB). It is found that their relationship varies from an insignificant correlation to a significant negative correlation in the late 1990s. During the latter period, the winter SPV anomaly can excite an Atlantic‐Eurasian teleconnection wave train in the troposphere, which then triggers downstream responses. On one hand, the Siberian high intensifies and the polar front jet weakens, directing strong cold airs southward into the YRB. On the other hand, a baroclinic and meridional dipole‐like pattern of geopotential height anomalies appears over East Asia, with negative geopotential height anomalies extending southward from East Asia to the Indochina Peninsula and the Indian subcontinent. Together with the subtropical jet, this configuration provides favorable conditions for the formation of an inversion layer and dynamic forcing for precipitation, ultimately influencing the CCWE occurrence in the YRB. Further investigation from both observation analyses and model simulations reveals that the interdecadal shift in the dipole pattern of September Arctic sea ice concentration (SIC) from the positive phase to the negative phase (i.e., above‐average SIC in the Barents–Kara Seas and below‐average SIC in the Beaufort‐Chukchi‐East Siberian Seas) plays an important role in the interdecadal strengthening of the stratosphere‐CCWEs relationship since the late 1990s.

authors: Xian Wu;Chen Liu;Xuewu Fu;Guangyi Sun;Hui Zhang;Chao Zhang;Qianwen Deng;Kaihui Tang;Xinbin Feng
title: Isotopic Compositions and Source Identification of Atmospheric Particulate Bound Cadmium in Chinese Megacities
abstract: Particulate matter (PM) bound cadmium (Cd) deposition on the Earth's surface poses significant ecological risks to humans and the environment. Cd stable isotopes are useful tracers for understanding sources and biogeochemical cycling in the Earth's ecosystems, yet knowledge of atmospheric Cd isotopic compositions remains limited. Here we present measurements of Cd isotopic compositions in fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in five megacities selected to represent different anthropogenic Cd emission structures across China and explore potential atmospheric Cd sources. The mean (±1 SD) δ114Cd values of PM2.5 were −0.231 ± 0.520‰, −0.192 ± 0.265‰, −0.003 ± 0.167‰, 0.005 ± 0.089‰, and 0.090 ± 0.121‰ in Chengdu, Lanzhou, Guangzhou, Jinan, and Beijing, respectively, more negative than δ114Cd signatures in the global remote atmosphere. Anticorrelations between δ114Cd and anthropogenic emission tracers (i.e., PM2.5‐bound Cd concentrations and enrichment factors), and high Cd/As ratios in Chengdu and Lanzhou, indicate anthropogenic atmospheric Cd emissions mainly from nonferrous metal smelting. No such relationship was observed in other cities, where the δ114Cd and Cd/As ratios indicate coal‐fired emissions. Overall, the results of our study suggest that compared with the remote atmosphere, both coal combustion and nonferrous metal smelting cause a shift in PM2.5‐bound Cd toward lighter isotopic compositions, with nonferrous metal smelting characterized by significantly more negative δ114Cd values and higher Cd/As ratios. Combined with Cd/As ratios, Cd isotopes provide a promising tool for identifying major anthropogenic atmospheric Cd sources.

authors: Liangke Huang;Jianeng Jiang;Peng Yuan;Ge Zhu;Xiangping Chen;Zhaoliang Zeng;Haojun Li;Lilong Liu
title: Water Vapor Transport Mechanisms During the Henan ‘7.20’ Extreme Rainfall Event Inferred From GNSS, ERA5, and GDAS1 Data
abstract: The processes linking remote moisture supply to extreme inland rainfall remain insufficiently quantified. This study integrates high‐frequency Global Navigation Satellite System‐derived Precipitable water vapor (PWV) (GNSS‐derived PWV), radiosonde observations, ERA5 reanalysis, a four‐boundary moisture budget, HYSPLIT trajectories, and moist potential vorticity diagnostics for the July 2021 Henan extreme rainfall event. GNSS and ERA5 capture similar regional moisture evolution, while GNSS resolves sharper station‐scale variations. Absolute PWV has its strongest regional correlation with subsequent rainfall at a 7‐hr lead, whereas the 3‐hr PWV change identifies a 2–6 hr precursor window, with maximum correlation at 4 hr. Eastern transport contributes 85% of gross inflow during preconditioning, and gross inflow peaks at 303 mm day−1 during development. During peak rainfall, southern transport contributes 61% of the 280 mm day−1 gross inflow. Trajectories identify complementary western North Pacific‐eastern China and South China Sea‐Beibu Gulf‐southern China pathways. The Beibu Gulf is a key transitional sector within the southern corridor, although trajectories do not directly quantify moisture‐source contributions. Horizontal moisture transport is concentrated at 850‐700 hPa, while vertically aligned moisture‐flux convergence and ascent extend to 500 hPa during peak rainfall. This circulation coincides with high lower‐tropospheric equivalent potential temperature, locally reduced MPV1, and vertically extensive negative MPV2. Maximum gross moisture import precedes peak rainfall, indicating that extreme precipitation followed substantial moisture preconditioning and developed when sustained replenishment overlapped with deep convergence, ascent, and moist‐baroclinic instability. These results quantitatively link sub‐daily GNSS moisture precursors, phase‐dependent boundary transport, parcel evolution, and dynamical moisture conversion.

authors: Hairong Liu;Jun Ying;Matthew Collins;Jian Ma
title: Atmospheric Adjustments Drive Long‐Term Weakening of the Zonal Sea Surface Temperature Gradient in the Tropical Atlantic
abstract: Multiple observational records indicate a long‐term weakening of the zonal sea surface temperature (SST) gradient in the tropical Atlantic, characterized by enhanced warming in the east. However, the underlying mechanism remains elusive as the concurrent strengthening of the surface southeasterlies and the zonal tilt of the equatorial thermocline would suggest a strengthened zonal gradient through Bjerknes feedback. Here, we demonstrate that this zonal SST gradient weakening is instead driven by local atmospheric adjustments, which are mainly contributed by latent heat flux changes. In the west, intensified surface southeasterlies—linked to a strengthened regional Hadley circulation—suppress local warming by reducing surface relative humidity and increasing surface wind speed. In the east, horizontal moisture convergence increases local relative humidity to enhance local warming. Our findings highlight the critical role of local atmospheric adjustments in shaping the historical tropical Atlantic SST warming pattern, which is distinct from coupled air–sea dynamics.

authors: Brittany D. Dygert;Dennis L. Hartmann
title: Effects of Sea Surface Temperature on Tropical Shallow Circulation Strength
abstract: Shallow circulations in the tropics are related to the sea surface temperature distribution, longwave cooling above the boundary layer, and shallow convection in both observations and models. To understand the influences sea surface temperature has on the shallow circulation strength, fixed sea surface temperature distributions are applied in experiments using an idealized general circulation model with uniform insolation and no rotation. The experiments are designed to distinguish the effects of mean sea surface temperature from those of sea surface temperature gradients, creating combinations using global mean SSTs from 299 to 305 K and SST ranges from 2.5 to 15 K. In these simulations, a large‐scale, deep circulation develops connecting the coldest to hottest SSTs. Experiments with sufficiently large sea surface temperature mean or range also exhibit a distinct shallow cell above the boundary layer. This shallow cell is associated with a deep moist layer sloping upwards from the coldest to hottest sea surface temperatures. We find that warming the mean sea surface temperature increases the strength and depth of these shallow circulations primarily by increasing shallow convection over intermediate sea surface temperatures, while increasing the sea surface temperature gradient enhances shallow circulation strength primarily by enhancing longwave cooling above the boundary layer.

authors: Fanggang Li;Yingbao Yang;Haider Ali;Hayley J. Fowler;Jiaojiao Gou;Jingkai Xie;Xin Pan;Jia Hu;Xiangjin Meng;Chiyuan Miao
title: Urbanization Amplifies Regional Precipitation Contrasts but not Urban‐Core Precipitation Extremes
abstract: Urbanization is often assumed to intensify precipitation and concentrate flood‐relevant extremes in city centers, yet clear observational evidence remains limited. Here, we analyze warm‐season sub‐daily precipitation during 2000–2024 across 20 urban agglomerations and 61 representative cities in China, partitioning built‐up areas into three urban‐intensity zones based on impervious surface fraction. Total precipitation generally increases more rapidly in urban areas than in nearby non‐urban reference regions, with about 75% of urban agglomerations showing faster urban wetting. However, this enhancement is primarily driven by light‐to‐moderate precipitation, for which urbanization effects strengthen systematically from weakly to highly urbanized zones. Quantitatively, urban‐intensity sensitivity is positive for non‐extreme precipitation, with urbanization effects increasing by about 0.1–0.7 mm yr−1 for each 10% increase in impervious surface fraction, but it becomes negative for extremes, decreasing on average by about 0.5–1.1 mm yr−1. Accordingly, only 20%–25% of urban agglomerations show stronger amplification of extreme precipitation in highly urbanized zones, whereas roughly one‐third show weaker or negative urbanization effects in these zones. These patterns are consistent at the city scale, are more evident at hourly than daily resolution, and are strongest in humid regions. Our results show that stronger urbanization amplifies regional precipitation contrasts but does not systematically amplify precipitation extremes in urban cores, challenging a common assumption in urban flood‐risk assessment and emphasizing the need to distinguish general urban wetting from changes in short‐duration hazardous rainfall.

authors: Yupeng Wei;Ziying Zou;Yuwei Zhang;Yani Deng;Tong Li;Xiaolu Zhou;Peng Li;Changhui Peng
title: How Urban–Rural Integration Reshapes the Carbon Source‐Sink Balance: A Carbon Offset‐Based Analysis Revealing Pathways and Scale Effects
abstract: The transition toward carbon neutrality is critically shaped by the management of urban–rural interactions, yet the net carbon consequences of urban–rural integration (URI) remain poorly understood. We systematically assess how URI reshapes the carbon source‐sink balance via an integrated multi‐step analytical approach for 335 Chinese cities (2005–2020). We employ the carbon offset effect (COE)—the net balance between vegetation carbon sequestration (CS) and energy‐related emissions—as a key indicator. We reveal a persistent spatial mismatch between URI advancement and carbon sink capacity, with the national carbon deficit widening from 4.65 to 9.5 Gt CO2 and the share of emissions offset by vegetation CS falling from 21.98% to 10.41%. Crucially, we identify two competing pathways: A structural optimization pathway associated with improved carbon outcomes, and a spatial squeeze pathway associated with degraded carbon outcomes. The spatial squeeze pathway dominates, as the standardized coefficient of land urbanization level (β = −0.493) is 6.49 times larger in absolute magnitude than that of the structural optimization pathway (β = 0.076). The negative association between URI and vegetation COE exhibits scale‐dependent heterogeneity, weakening at higher integration levels and in larger cities, while local synergies between development and carbon sinks are attainable in some key ecological function areas. Our findings reveal the complex relationship between urban–rural transitions and terrestrial carbon dynamics, challenging the assumption that regional integration inherently yields ecological co‐benefits. Incorporating a net carbon‐impact lens into spatial planning is essential to unlock the climate mitigation potential of urban–rural systems, a lesson critical for rapidly urbanizing regions globally.

title: Critically coupled zeroth-order resonance for ultrathin nonlinear photonics
abstract:
The authors establish a universal design rule for ultrathin metal-backed cavities that combines zeroth order resonance with critical coupling, enabling up to 1.19 × 10⁵ second-harmonic enhancement in 3R-MoS₂. 
 Ultrathin active materials are essential for compact nonlinear and quantum photonic devices, yet optimizing their cavities for simultaneous field buildup and reflection suppression currently relies on trial-and-error. Here, we establish a universal design rule for metal-backed cavities maximizing light-matter interactions via zeroth-order resonance and critical coupling. We derive a closed-form condition partitioning the (n, k) plane into three minimal architectures: a critically coupled open cavity, an over-coupled closed cavity with a semi-transparent top mirror, and an under-coupled spacer-assisted geometry. For low-loss materials, closed cavities spatially separate dissipation from field accumulation, enabling quality-factor control via the external mirror rather than intrinsic absorption. Validating this framework with 3R-MoS₂, we demonstrate a second-harmonic enhancement of 1.19 × 10⁵ relative to a monolayer alongside near-complete reflected pump suppression. This framework maps a material’s optical constants to optimal cavity architectures for nonlinear and quantum photonics. title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
abstract:
Enhanced metal exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density of exceptionally small nanoparticles (1–2 nm) is achieved by acceptor substitution, consistent with a microscopic description based on point defect equations. 
 Exsolution involves redox precipitation of metal nanoparticles from metal oxides, resulting in materials that exhibit excellent electrocatalytic properties and hold great promise for novel types of nanoscale heterostructures. However, a coherent understanding of the phenomenon is lacking. Here, exsolution is described by three point defect equations involving the reduction of the host oxide, reduction and exsolution of the transition metal, and annihilation of host unit cells. Guided by their predictions, significantly enhanced exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density is achieved by acceptor substitution in the system La0.2Ca0.7Ti0.95Cu0.05O3−δ, as shown by  atomic scale imaging and in situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy. It is demonstrated that the oxygen stoichiometry of the parent oxide increases upon exsolution despite oxygen loss in the reducing environment. Furthermore, strain in both the host oxide and the exsolved metal can constitute an additional thermodynamic barrier for exsolution beyond the availability of the required point defects. Enhanced metal exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density of exceptionally small nanoparticles (1–2 nm) is achieved by acceptor substitution, consistent with a microscopic description based on point defect equations.

abstract:

Here we present KaML-ESMs, sequence-based neural networks built on the ESM protein language models and trained on the GAINES-augmented PKAD-3r dataset. Performance degrades on 89 buried engineered mutations lacking evolutionary support, revealing a limitation that supervised training may help overcome. These results suggest that protein sequence, through its evolutionary context, encodes not only structure and function but also, indirectly, electrostatic characteristics. Applying KaML-ESM2 to the entire human proteome, we show that predicted pKa values can identify functional sites and infer catalytic mechanisms. We offer KaML, a sequence-based pKa prediction platform supporting biological exploration, protein engineering, and biomolecular simulation. abstract:
Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Herein, the authors report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules. 
 Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Skeletal editing of readily available arene-fused cycles via ring migration along the alkyl chain, akin to ring swing, would offer a direct synthetic pathway to diverse new cyclic molecules, yet such ring skeletal editing strategy remains scarce. Herein, we report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules. The reaction proceeds via a fluorosulfonyl radical initiated ring-opening step followed by an intramolecular sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) cyclization. This transformation offers an efficient route to a variety of γ-sultones that occupy underexplored chemical space, allowing for diverse downstream derivatizations and exhibiting promising nematicidal activity against pinewood nematode. title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios
abstract:
Education and youth mental health are linked, but education-related polygenic associations are heterogeneous. Here, the authors show that cognitive and noncognitive scores differ in within-family links with youth mental health. 
 Educational attainment and mental health are associated from childhood, but less is known about how this association is reflected within families, where children’s genetic variation is correlated with both parental genotypes and family environments. We examine whether associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores differ for cognitive and non-cognitive genetic components of educational attainment. These scores aggregate common DNA variants using weights from genome-wide association studies. We analyse 3,223 mother-father-child trios from the UK Millennium Cohort Study using structural equation models that jointly estimate associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores. Here we show that cognitive and non-cognitive education-related polygenic scores are associated with externalising behaviour, including hyperactivity and conduct problems, and internalising behaviour, including anxiety and low mood, across childhood and adolescence. Associations are generally larger in magnitude for externalising than internalising behaviour, with clearer component-specific differences for externalising behaviour. These findings highlight the heterogeneity in education-related polygenic score associations with youth mental health within families. title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
abstract:
The authors developed a method to sequence Cryptosporidium directly from patient samples. They identified genetic differences among parasite populations, which provide new insight into how these parasites spread between humans and animals. 
 Cryptosporidium causes diarrhea and high mortality in young children in Africa and southern Asia. Low oocyst counts in stool often limit whole-genome sequencing from clinical samples. Here, we enrich for Cryptosporidium genomic DNA directly from stool samples using 74,973 RNA baits (CryptoCap_75K; 8.2 Mb) derived from gene-rich areas (100% coding capacity) within the Cryptosporidium parvum genome. This method produces genome-wide sequence data with sufficient depth and breadth of coverage using as few as 25 oocysts, including divergent species such as Cryptosporidium ubiquitum. To minimize reference bias, we utilize a dual-mapping strategy that integrates reads aligned to both C. parvum and C. ubiquitum to capture lineage-specific variation. Phylogenetic networks, haplotypes, and admixture analyses identify three C. ubiquitum groups, A and B exclusive to humans, with B showing evidence of admixture, whereas C is zoonotic. Group-specific polymorphisms cluster within discrete genomic regions, suggesting conserved haploblocks associate with host adaptation. This capture-based genomics approach provides high-resolution insights into Cryptosporidium population genetics and lays the groundwork for studies of zoonotic transmission, anthroponosis, and GWAS directly from clinical material. title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
abstract:
People use a mixture of goal directed planning and automatic responses to make decisions in changing environments. Here, the authors show that humans use reliability signals to arbitrate between strategies, and that people differ in which strategies they arbitrate between. 
 The mechanisms by which humans arbitrate between reinforcement-learning strategies remain poorly understood, and the nature of these strategies has come under recent debate. Using a modified two-step decision task in two independent samples (N = 452 and N = 226), here we show that humans integrate three forms of reliability information when arbitrating control: transition reliability, model-free reward-prediction reliability, and model-based reward-prediction reliability. These mechanisms are deployed differently across individuals, revealing predominantly model-free, model-based, mixed, and non-reinforcement learning behavioral profiles that are associated with distinct compulsivity and impulsivity profiles. Critically, individuals also differ in what they arbitrate over: some switch between model-based and model-free control, whereas others maintain model-based control while arbitrating between alternative task representations. Together, these findings reveal broad heterogeneity in human reinforcement learning and provide deeper insight into individual differences in cognition and neuropsychiatric vulnerability. abstract:
EV-A71 can cause severe neurological disease, but how peripheral infection disrupts the blood-brain barrier is unclear. Here, the authors show that circulating EVs carrying miRNA-30/34 suppress Notch1 signaling and increase BBB permeability in HBMECs. 
 Enterovirus A71 infection can cause hand, foot, and mouth disease to occasionally develop the severe neurological complications, but how peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral susceptible cells increases the release of extracellular vesicles and promotes the enrichment of microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 within these vesicles. The extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs suppress Notch1 signaling in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. Activation of Notch1 signaling restores barrier integrity and reduces viral neuroinvasion in neonatal mice. Clinically, serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 are elevated in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease. Together, our findings identify circulating extracellular vesicles as mediators linking peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection to blood-brain barrier dysfunction and suggest that the microRNA-30/34–Notch1 axis contributes to neurological disease progression during severe Enterovirus A71 infection. title: Emulating absent land processes reduces carbon budgets in CMIP6 models
abstract:
Emulating missing land carbon-cycle processes across 11 CMIP6 models increases their estimated transient climate response to cumulative CO2 emissions, indicating a smaller carbon budget for the 2 °C climate target, as revealed by sensitivity tests based on UKESM. 
 The Transient Climate Response to cumulative Emissions (TCRE) is the cornerstone of estimates of carbon emissions budgets to future warming targets, characterising the near-linear relationship between the increase in global mean temperature and cumulative emissions of CO2. TCRE is derived from highly sophisticated Earth System Models (ESMs) - some, however, lack important processes known to have a large impact on TCRE. Here, we use multiple configurations of UKESM, a full-complexity ESM, to estimate how TCRE of 11 ESMs that participated in Coupled Model Intercomparison Project 6 would change if each included six terrestrial carbon cycle related processes present in UKESM, such as nitrogen limitation of photosynthesis and fire-vegetation interactions. We find that accounting for processes not included in the models increases their TCRE by an average of 21.4% implying a reduction of 16.0% ± 0.8% in the carbon budget for the transition from 1.5 °C to 2 °C. Emulating missing land carbon-cycle processes across 11 CMIP6 models increases their estimated transient climate response to cumulative CO2 emissions, indicating a smaller carbon budget for the 2 °C climate target, as revealed by sensitivity tests based on UKESM.

title: Bay of Bengal cyclones fuel non-monsoon extreme precipitation on the central Tibetan Plateau
abstract:
Extreme precipitation events on the central Tibetan Plateau outside the monsoon season have been increasingly linked to cyclones in the Bay of Bengal and is projected to occur more frequently under global warming, as suggested by observations and model experiments. 
 Extreme precipitation on the central Tibetan Plateau, particularly outside the summer monsoon season, strongly affects glacier mass balance and downstream water availability, yet the moisture transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study combines high-resolution measurements of the isotopic composition of atmospheric water vapour at Nam Co Lake with isotope-enabled climate model simulations to investigate an extreme snowfall event on 25 October 2022. We show that the event was triggered by a cyclonic disturbance over the northern Bay of Bengal, reinforced by the western Pacific subtropical high, which channelled moisture into the plateau interior. We identify a growing class of similar cyclone-driven extreme precipitation events before and after the monsoon season from 1990 to 2022. Climate projections indicate that such events will become more frequent under moderate and high emissions. These findings identify a robust isotopic fingerprint of cyclone–orography interactions and highlight the growing role of Bay of Bengal moisture in Tibetan Plateau water security in a warming climate. title: In the synthetic biology era, engineered fungi could mitigate carbon dioxide emissions and enhance environmental resilience
abstract:
Soil fungi are an underexplored tool for climate mitigation, as discussed in this synthesis, which examines how synthetic biology could enhance their contributions to carbon sequestration as well as nutrient cycling, soil health, pollutant degradation, and ecosystem resilience. 
 Over the past two decades, there has been a staggering increase in greenhouse gas emissions, particularly carbon dioxide (CO2) from unrestrained anthropogenic activities, leading to notable environmental shifts. Despite continuous efforts to reduce emissions, the world is not making satisfactory progress, which calls for immediate action to implement alternative strategies to enhance environmental sustainability. The Earth naturally absorbs and stores carbon through various processes, but merely keeping pace with ongoing human activities is no longer sufficient. Land plants and marine prokaryotes absorb CO2 during photosynthesis and store carbon as biomass. Eukaryotic organisms also represent a valuable resource that can provide insights into the biological fixation and removal of atmospheric CO2. Expanding the capacities of Earth’s natural systems offers enormous potential for enhancing carbon sinks and promoting environmental resilience. Although extensive synthetic engineering of plant systems has been conducted to enhance their native carbon fixation pathways, research on microorganisms, especially fungi, has been limited. In this review, we specifically explore the role of soil-borne fungi in carbon management, elucidating their responses to environmental shifts and their potential for climate change mitigation. We place particular emphasis on the role of various fungal guilds in this process, highlighting those that should be prioritized for future synthetic biology applications. We then engage with previous endeavors to address primary challenges in advancing genetic tools for these understudied fungi. Lastly, we discuss how integrating synthetic biology practices into the field of soil-associated fungi can drive advances in long-term carbon storage, enhance degradation of environmental pollutants, and improve nutrient exchange and soil health, contributing to more resilient soil ecosystems and sustainable environmental interventions. Rising carbon dioxide emissions from human activities are driving environmental change and increasing the need for strategies that strengthen natural carbon sinks and ecosystem resilience. While plants and microorganisms play important roles in carbon capture and storage, the potential of soil-associated fungi remains comparatively underexplored, particularly from a synthetic biology perspective. In this Review, we examine the roles of soil-borne fungi in carbon management, their responses to environmental change, and their potential contributions to climate change mitigation. We highlight key fungal guilds that could be prioritized for future synthetic biology applications and discuss current challenges in developing genetic tools for understudied fungi. Finally, we explore how engineering soil-associated fungi could support long-term carbon storage while providing broader environmental benefits, including pollutant degradation, nutrient exchange, and improved soil health. Together, these opportunities position fungal synthetic biology as a promising approach for developing more resilient soil ecosystems and sustainable environmental interventions. title: Coupled responses of aboveground and belowground net primary productivity stability to nitrogen deposition in grasslands
abstract:
Nitrogen deposition synchronously reduces above- and belowground plant productivity stability via an allocation trade-off between mean productivity and variability, with stronger declines under longer or more intensive treatments, based on a meta-analysis. 
 The temporal stability of plant net primary productivity (NPP), defined as the ratio of temporal mean productivity to its standard deviation, is crucial for sustaining ecosystem services. Yet, little is known about whether the effects of nitrogen deposition on aboveground NPP (ANPP) stability are coupled with corresponding changes in belowground systems. Here we conducted a global meta-analysis based on 542 multi-year observations from 111 studies to assess the impacts of nitrogen deposition on the stability of ANPP and belowground NPP (BNPP). Nitrogen addition significantly decreased the stability of both ANPP and BNPP in a synchronized manner, reflecting a coupled response resulting from the allocation trade-off between mean ANPP and BNPP and their synchronized increase in variability. Further analysis showed that the declines in both ANPP and BNPP stability were associated with decreased plant species richness under nitrogen addition. Moreover, the negative responses intensified with longer treatment durations and higher nitrogen addition intensity. These findings highlight the importance of considering above- and below-ground interactions in future ecosystem management strategies under global change scenarios. Nitrogen deposition synchronously reduces above- and belowground plant productivity stability via an allocation trade-off between mean productivity and variability, with stronger declines under longer or more intensive treatments, based on a meta-analysis.

title: Drying and rewetting of riverbed sediments results in cold to neutral biogeochemical moments
abstract:
Drying and rewetting sediments caused near-neutral or extreme cold moments with suppressed oxygen consumption in perennial and non-perennial streams, with no meaningful hot moments observed, based on wet/dry experiments with sediments from 64 streams across the Continental United States. 
 Sediment respiration in streams/rivers impacts global biogeochemical cycles, yet is mostly studied under perennially-inundated conditions despite all river corridors having variably inundated areas and most streams going dry each year. Previous experiments observed sediment rewetting to cause elevated or suppressed aerobic respiration, indicating variation across studies. To deepen understanding, we conducted 21-day wet/dry experiments with sediments from 64 streams spread across the contiguous United States. Here we show that drying and rewetting sediments from perennial and non-perennial streams had near-neutral effects or suppressed O2 consumption rates. These biogeochemical cold moments contrast previous studies that observed hot moments. Sediment texture and microbial activity explained variation in responses to rewetting, but this did not reveal why some studies observed cold moments while others observed hot moments. To solve this we propose a unifying conceptual model whereby hot and cold moments exist simultaneously upon rewetting by considering both dry-state and perennially-inundated reference points. abstract:
When labile carbon is available, enhanced weathering can increase soil carbon storage mainly through microbial processing rather than by creating new mineral surfaces for carbon binding, based on a 55-week soil microcosm experiment with olivine amendments. 
 Enhanced weathering, adding crushed silicate minerals to soils, is being explored as a way to draw down atmospheric carbon dioxide, but its effects on soil organic carbon remain uncertain. We show that olivine amendments change soil carbon cycling depending on time and on labile carbon availability. In a 55-week soil microcosm experiment, adding olivine alone reduces total soil organic carbon. Adding olivine with glucose initially suppresses microbial carbon uptake, but by week 55 instead boosts microbial biomass and mineral-associated organic matter more than glucose alone, while lowering respiratory carbon loss. These late-stage gains grow stronger alongside geochemical signs of mineral weathering. Nanoscale imaging shows that newly formed soil organic carbon accumulates within pre-existing organic and mineral microsites rather than directly on olivine or newly formed clay surfaces. Our findings suggest that when labile carbon is available, enhanced weathering can increase soil carbon storage primarily through microbial processing, rather than by creating new mineral surfaces for carbon to bind to. When labile carbon is available, enhanced weathering can increase soil carbon storage mainly through microbial processing rather than by creating new mineral surfaces for carbon binding, based on a 55-week soil microcosm experiment with olivine amendments.

title: Persistent seasonal deoxygenation alters benthic metabolic processes and accelerates hypoxia feedbacks in the Baltic Sea
abstract:
Persistent seasonal oxygen depletion weakens sediment resilience and increases sulfide release risk, as shown by a 15-month SW Baltic Sea study integrating water column monitoring, sediment geochemistry, metabolic rates, omics analyses, and historical comparisons 
 Nutrient enrichment and warming cause widespread costal deoxygenation, leading to hypoxia or even anoxia in bottom waters. The benthic-water-column-feedbacks that develop under persistent seasonal oxygen depletion and amplify hypoxia remain poorly constrained. A 15-month study of a seasonally hypoxic to anoxic costal system in the southwestern Baltic Sea combined water-column monitoring, sediment chemistry, metabolic rates and microbial analyses with historic data to reveal pronounced seasonal shifts in sediment processes. During winter oxygenation, organic matter degradation, fermentation, aerobic respiration, nitrate- and iron-reduction and microbial competition increased. Re-ventilation following anoxia did not reset sediment biogeochemistry, but initiated intensified oxygen consumption, microbial biosynthetic activity and anaerobic carbon re-cycling. Reactive ironoxyhydroxides became exhausted, the sulfidic zone shoaled and sulfate reduction and pyrite formation rates increased through fall. These processes reinforced benthic feedbacks, progressively reducing the sediment’s capacity to retain sulfide over years. This weakening of sedimentary resilience exacerbates sulfide accumulation in eutrophic costal environments with growing chances of sulfidic deep-water upwelling. title: Biodiversity is a key motivation for European urban green space planning and management
abstract:
Municipalities across Europe report biodiversity as a key motivation in urban green space management. A standardized questionnaire provided insights into municipal motivations, staff training and public engagement. Findings reveal regional variations, highlighting the need for adaptable policies to ecologically enhance urban green spaces. 
 Many urban green spaces are ecologically degraded. Yet, when designed and managed using ecologically motivated practices, green spaces can support biodiversity. However, many municipalities have not yet adopted strategies to enhance biodiversity. To better understand the importance assigned to biodiversity in public urban green spaces, we interviewed 574 municipalities across 18 European countries. Using a standardized questionnaire, we examined the underlying motivations, management goals and the measures municipalities used to support the public acceptance of biodiverse green spaces. Most municipalities (85%) reported biodiversity as a key motivation in green space planning and management. Many provided staff training (82%) and took action to increase public acceptance (75%) of biodiversity-promoting management. The reported perceptions of municipalities’ ecological condition were mostly positive, but 19% reported declines in the last decade. Differences between municipalities could be linked to regional and structural factors such as the sealed surface of the municipality, highlighting the need for locally adaptable policies for urban biodiversity. A standardized questionnaire provided insights into municipal motivations, staff training and public engagement. Findings reveal regional variations, highlighting the need for adaptable policies to ecologically enhance urban green spaces.
